title.ko: 1강. 하고 · (이)랑 · 와/과: 동반과 나열, 한 강에서 같이

blocks.md:
In Korean, **the exact same connector particle** performs **two different roles**:

1. **Companion (“Together with someone”)**:
   - *“친구**하고** 영화를 봤어요.”* *(I watched a movie **with** a friend.)*
   - *“동생**이랑** 밥을 먹어요.”* *(I eat **with** my sibling.)*
   - *“선생님**과** 상담했어요.”* *(I had a meeting **with** my teacher.)*

2. **Listing Nouns (“And / As well as”)**:
   - *“밥**하고** 김치를 먹었어요.”* *(I ate rice **and** kimchi.)*
   - *“커피**랑** 빵을 샀어요.”* *(I bought coffee **and** bread.)*
   - *“한국**과** 미국”* *(Korea **and** America)*

Because the grammar and particle forms are **100% identical**, you learn them together as one unified tool!

**Register & Batchim Rules:**

- **하고 (Everyday Spoken, Universal)**:
  - Attaches directly to **any noun**, with or without batchim! (친구하고, 밥하고)

- **(이)랑 (Casual Spoken, Friendly)**:
  - Vowel ending → **-랑** (*친구랑, 커피랑*)
  - Batchim ending → **-이랑** (*밥이랑, 선생님이랑*)

- **와 / 과 (Formal Written, 문어체)**:
  - Vowel ending → **-와** (*친구와, 사과와*)
  - Batchim ending → **-과** (*학생과, 한국과*)

items.tip: I watched a movie with a friend. (하고: Companion)
I ordered coffee and bread. (랑: Casual listing)
Conversation between student and teacher. (과: Formal)

blocks.q: In a formal business essay or news article, which particle should you attach to 학생 (student, batchim ends in ㅇ) to mean "students and teachers"?
blocks.why: In formal written Korean (문어체), nouns with batchim take 과: 학생과 선생님. (와 is for vowel endings, and 하고/이랑 are spoken register).

blocks.q: You are chatting casually with a close friend about your lunch: "I ate rice and soup." What is the natural casual spoken phrasing for 밥 (rice)?
blocks.why: 밥 ends in consonant ㅂ, so casual spoken (이)랑 becomes -이랑: 밥이랑 국을 먹었어요.

blocks.q: What are the two different roles that "친구하고" can have in a sentence?
options: Companion (with a friend) and Listing (a friend and someone else)
Giving to a friend and receiving from a friend
blocks.why: 하고, (이)랑, and 와/과 serve both as companion ("with") and noun listing ("and").

blocks.meaning: Yesterday at the department store, I bought pants and a shirt.
blocks.why: Listing two nouns (pants and a shirt) takes 하고 (or 와/과, 이랑).

blocks.q: Put in order: "I watched a movie with a friend on the weekend."
Match each noun with its correct formal written connector (와/과):

blocks.wrong: 문어체 받침 오류: 선생님와 면담을 진행했습니다.
blocks.hint: For nouns ending in a batchim (선생님), use 과 instead of 와: 선생님과.
blocks.why: Batchim nouns take 과 in formal written style: 선생님과 면담을 진행했습니다.

blocks.q: Spoken: "I watched a movie with my friend."

blocks.say: 주말에 친구하고 같이 맛있는 밥을 먹었어요.

title.ko: 2강. (이)나: 선택과 수량 강조, 두 가지 다른 쓰임
title.en: Lesson 2. (이)나: Choice ("Or") vs. Quantity ("As much as")

blocks.md:
The particle **(이)나** has **two very distinct lives** depending on where it appears in a sentence:

1. **Choice (“Or / Either... or”)**:
   - Positioned between two nouns to suggest options (*“either A or B is fine”*):
   - *“커피**나** 차 드세요.”* *(Please have coffee **or** tea.)*
   - *“주말에는 영화**나** 독서를 해요.”* *(On weekends I watch movies **or** read.)*
   - *“밥**이나** 빵을 먹을까요?”* *(Shall we eat rice **or** bread?)*

2. **Quantity Emphasis (“As many as... / A whopping...!”)**:
   - Attached to a **counter or quantity number** (*3 cups, 10 hours, 5 people*).
   - Conveys **surprise or amazement that the amount is greater than expected**:
   - *“커피를 세 잔**이나** 마셨어요!”* *(I drank **as many as three whole cups** of coffee!)*
   - *“어제 10시간**이나** 잤어요.”* *(I slept a whopping **10 hours**!)*

**How to Distinguish at a Glance:**

- **Between two nouns?** → **Choice (“or”)**
  - Vowel ending: **-나** (*커피나 차, 영화나 운동*)
  - Batchim ending: **-이나** (*밥이나 빵, 책이나 잡지*)

- **Attached to a number / counter?** → **Quantity Emphasis (“as many as”)**
  - *3잔**이나** (3 whole cups!), 5개**나** (as many as 5!), 10명**이나** (10 whole people!)*

items.tip: Shall we have coffee or tea? (Choice: 나)
I slept a whopping 10 hours! (Quantity: 이나)
I ate as many as 5 apples! (Quantity: 나)

blocks.q: Your coworker asks what you want to drink. You say: "Please give me water or juice." Which particle attaches to 물 (water, ends in batchim)?
blocks.why: 물 ends in consonant ㄹ, so the choice particle is -이나: 물이나 주스 주세요. (물과 / 물하고 mean "water AND juice").

blocks.q: A friend says: "어제 커피를 세 잔이나 마셨어요!" What is the nuance of 세 잔이나?
options: Emphasizing surprise at how many cups were drunk (as many as 3 cups)
Offering a choice between three cups or two cups
Saying they only drank three cups and wanted more
Stating that they could not drink three cups
blocks.why: When (이)나 attaches after a number and counter (세 잔), it emphasizes that the quantity is unexpectedly large: "a whopping three cups!"

blocks.q: Choose the sentence where (이)나 expresses CHOICE ("or"):
blocks.why: 영화나 볼까요 suggests an option among leisure activities ("Shall we watch a movie or something?"). The others all emphasize high numbers.

blocks.meaning: Yesterday I was so tired that I slept as many as 10 hours.
blocks.why: 10시간 ends in consonant ㄴ, so the quantity emphasis particle is -이나: 10시간이나.

blocks.q: Put in order: "If you are thirsty, please drink water or juice."
Match each sentence with its correct (이)나 function:

blocks.wrong: 받침 오류: 점심에 밥나 라면을 먹을 거예요.
blocks.hint: 밥 ends in a batchim (ㅂ), so attach -이나 for choice: 밥이나.
blocks.why: Nouns with batchim take -이나: 밥이나 라면을 먹을 거예요.

blocks.q: Choice: "Please drink water or juice."
Read aloud with an amazed, expressive tone emphasizing 10시간이나:

title.ko: 3강. 도 · 마다 · 의: 자주 쓰는 나머지 셋
title.en: Lesson 3. 도, 마다, & 의: Also, Every, & Possessive

blocks.md:
Three final particles will complete your essential beginner grammar toolkit:

1. **도 (“Also / Too / Even”)**:
   - Expresses inclusion (*“me too, this too”*).
   - *“저**도** 학생이에요.”* *(I am also a student.)*
   - *“이것**도** 주세요.”* *(Please give me this too.)*

2. **마다 (“Every / Each”)**:
   - Marks recurring frequency or individual uniqueness without exception (*every day, each person*):
   - *“주말**마다** 운동을 해요.”* *(Every weekend I exercise.)*
   - *“나라**마다** 문화가 달라요.”* *(Culture differs by every country.)*
   - *“사람**마다** 생각이 달라요.”* *(Every person thinks differently.)*

3. **의 (“Possessive ’s / Of”)**:
   - Marks ownership or affiliation: *“선생님**의** 책”* *(The teacher’s book)*.
   - Pronounced **[에]** when used as a possessive marker!

**Two Must-Know Secrets:**

1. **도 REPLACES Subject & Object Markers!**
   - Never say *“저**는도**”* or *“사과**를도**”*!
   - `저 + 는 + 도` → **저도** (O)
   - `사과 + 를 + 도` → **사과도** (O)

2. **의 is ALMOST ALWAYS DROPPED in Spoken Korean!**
   - While English requires *“my friend”* or *“teacher’s car”*, Koreans simply say:
     - *“선생님**의** 책”* → *“**선생님 책**”*
     - *“저**의** 친구”* → *“**제 친구**”*
     - *“우리**의** 나라”* → *“**우리나라**”*
   - You will hear **의** in formal writing, speeches, and poetry, but daily speech drops it freely!

items.tip: I stroll in the park every weekend. (마다: Every)
Teacher’s warm words. (의: Possessive, spoken as [에])

blocks.q: You want to say: "I am also a student." Which sentence follows the correct particle replacement rule for 도?
blocks.why: 도 replaces topic/subject markers (은/는, 이/가). You cannot combine them into 저는도: 저도 학생이에요.

blocks.q: How is the possessive particle 의 typically handled in everyday conversational Korean?
options: It is pronounced [에], and is almost always omitted in casual speech (e.g. 제 친구, 선생님 책)
It must always be pronounced [의] with strong emphasis
It can only be used with inanimate objects
It changes to -로 when speaking casually
blocks.why: Possessive 의 is pronounced [에] in speech, and native speakers almost always omit it in everyday conversation (우리 집, 제 친구).

blocks.q: Complete the sentence expressing a regular weekend routine: "저는 주말(__) 산에 가요."
blocks.why: 마다 expresses regular recurring intervals ("every weekend"): 주말마다 산에 가요.

blocks.meaning: In every country, the way of greeting is different.
blocks.why: 마다 means "every / each": 나라마다 (in each/every country).

blocks.q: Put in order: "I also thought that movie was really fun."
Match each sentence with the particle’s meaning:

blocks.wrong: 조사 중복 오류: 저는도 한국 음식을 아주 좋아해요.
blocks.why: Do not combine 는 and 도 together. Use 저도: 저도 한국 음식을 아주 좋아해요.

blocks.q: Inclusion: "I also study Korean."

title.ko: 4강. 실전 비교: 나열과 선택(와 · 이나 · 마다 · 도) 총정리
title.en: Lesson 4. Summary & Practice: Listing & Selection Particles

blocks.md:
In this course, you learned essential particles for connecting nouns and expressing frequency:

1. **Listing & Companion (-와/과, -하고, -(이)랑)**: Connect nouns with 'and' or mean 'with'.
   - 사과**와** 배를 샀어요. *(I bought apples and pears.)*
   - 친구**하고** 영화를 봐요. *(I watch movies with a friend.)*

2. **Choice & Approximate / Wonder (-(이)나)**: Means 'or' between nouns, or emphasizes surprisingly large amounts.
   - 커피**나** 차를 마셔요. *(I drink coffee or tea.)*
   - 피자를 3판**이나** 먹었어요! *(I ate as many as 3 pizzas!)*

3. **Every (-마다) & Also (-도)**: Regular recurrence and addition.
   - 주말**마다** 운동해요. *(I exercise every weekend.)*
   - 저**도** 갈게요. *(I will go too.)*

items.tip: I go to the bookstore and read books every weekend. (주말마다 every weekend)
I took an enjoyable walk in the park with a friend. (친구와 with a friend)

items.ch: 목이 마르면 시원한 물이나 주스 드세요.
items.tip: If you are thirsty, please drink cool water or juice. (물이나 water or juice)

blocks.q: Connecting two nouns with "and": Noun ends with batchim ㄱ (책). Which particle correctly follows: "책(__) 공책"?
blocks.why: Nouns ending with a final consonant (batchim ㄱ in 책) take -과: 책과 공책.

blocks.sentence: 저는 주말[마다] 한강 공원에 가서 자전거를 타요.
blocks.meaning: I go to Hangang Park and ride a bicycle every weekend.
blocks.why: To express a recurring regular routine ("every weekend"), use -마다: 주말마다.

blocks.q: 도 replaces topic/subject particles. Correct the common beginner error 「저는도」 to just one word: 「___ 한국어 공부를 좋아해요. (I also like studying Korean.)」
blocks.why: The particle -도 completely replaces 는. Never say 저는도; use 저도.

blocks.q: A: "점심에 뭐 드실래요?" B: "시간이 없으니 간단하게 김밥(__) 라면 먹어요." (Suggesting choice: gimbap or ramen).
blocks.why: 김밥 ends in batchim ㅂ, so to express choice ('or'), attach -이나: 김밥이나 라면 먹어요.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "I also like that song really much."

blocks.say: 아침마다 따뜻한 커피나 차를 한잔 마셔요.
blocks.q: Read aloud comfortably describing your morning coffee or tea routine:
